title: GS21 BENCHMARK at a lower price of the aggregate productivity shock, gamma_x 0.1 instead of 0.5 (gs_vy at NY 1, no y): the baseline the low-gamma_x economies are read against
question: Does a priced second factor make a fair gap in GS21 when firm exposure runs through operating leverage (convex in profitability) instead of a level sort?
notes: 2026-10-23. Lever 3: shrink the additive base. gs_vy at NY = 1 and gs_bv = 0 is gs_solve_reg at gmreg [1, 1] (parity test), so this is gsbase with gamma_x 0.1.

changes: gs_fc 0.0: a fixed operating cost per unit capital (0 in gvy25 and gsbase)
the y factor moves the COST, exp(gs_bc y), with types gs_bc [0.0]; production exposure gs_bv 0, no level compensation (at y = 0 every type pays the same cost)
everything else gvy25's: 9-node priced y chain, gamma_v 2.5, kappa_y 0.35

method.gs_vy_exposure: cost-side: fixed cost gs_fc * exp(gs_bc y)

seeds.policy: run_oracle.py --seed drives BOTH the firm-level shocks and the aggregate y path (reg_seed offset by the seed).
